title: Augment Mixture Design
selectedvars: Select mixture components (2+ numeric columns) from the EXISTING design
lblExistingNote: The active dataset must be your EXISTING mixture design (the runs you have already run or plan to run). These rows are kept fixed -- they are never removed or changed. By default, bounds for any new points are derived automatically from the minimum and maximum of each selected component in this existing data -- see the Manual Bounds Override section below for when to supply your own instead.
totalAmount: Total amount (must match the units already used in the existing design)
lowerBoundsInput: Lower bounds (comma-separated, same order as components selected above)
upperBoundsInput: Upper bounds (comma-separated, same order as components selected above)
lblBoundsOverrideNote: Leave BOTH fields blank to automatically use the existing design's own min/max per component -- reliable when the existing design came from Create Mixture Design (Simplex Lattice, Simplex Centroid, or Extreme Vertices), since all three always include the true boundary points. Specify BOTH fields (in the same units as Total amount, e.g. '20,10,20,15') if the existing design came from a D-optimal search -- D-optimal point selection is not guaranteed to touch every true extreme, so the auto-derived range can be narrower than originally intended -- or if you want to search a different region than the existing design happens to span. Compare the printed derived bounds in the output against your originally intended constraints; if they don't match, override them here. You cannot specify only one of the two fields.
lblTargetModel: Target Model to Support After Augmentation
linearChk: Linear Scheffé model — main effects only
quadChk: Quadratic Scheffé model — main effects + all pairwise component interactions
cubicChk: Special Cubic Scheffé model — quadratic + all three-way component products
lblTargetModelNote: The minimum number of total runs required for the selected model is computed automatically from the number of components and checked against 'Total number of runs after augmentation' below before the search runs.
numOfRunsAfter: Total number of runs AFTER augmentation (including the existing design's runs)
candidateLevels: Candidate grid resolution (levels per component axis)
candidateLevelsHelp: Controls how finely the region spanned by the existing design is discretized when searching for new points. Use an ODD value (default: 11) so the candidate grid can represent an exact 50/50 binary blend (Total/2) -- an even value cannot include that exact halfway point.
numOfOptiRepeats: Number of optimization repeats (default increased to 15 -- augmentation with existing rows frozen is a harder search than a fresh D-optimal selection, especially for higher-order terms the existing design has no information for)
lbl1: You may not need to change the randomization settings
randomizationChk: Randomize the run order (of the full combined design, existing + new)

help.title: Augment Mixture Design
help.r_help: help(optFederov, package = AlgDesign) -- see the 'augment' and 'rows' arguments
help.body:
Description
Adds D-optimal additional runs to an existing mixture design, keeping all of the existing design's runs fixed — unlike Create D-Optimal Mixture Design, which always builds a completely new design from scratch with no memory of prior runs. Use this dialog when you have already collected data at your existing design's points and want to add more runs to support a higher-order model, without discarding the data you already have.

Why "Create D-Optimal Mixture Design" can't do this
That dialog always selects its final run set from scratch out of a fresh candidate grid — nothing marks your prior runs as "keep these." This dialog instead uses AlgDesign::optFederov()'s augment=TRUE and rows= arguments directly, which freeze a specified set of rows and search only for the best additional points to add to them.

How enough runs are guaranteed for your target model
Select the model you ultimately want to fit in Analyze Mixture Design (Linear, Quadratic, or Special Cubic). The minimum number of total runs that model requires is computed automatically from the number of components:
  • Linear: q parameters
  • Quadratic: q + C(q,2) parameters
  • Special Cubic: q + C(q,2) + C(q,3) parameters
where q is the number of components and C(q,2)/C(q,3) are the number of pairwise/three-way component combinations. If "Total number of runs after augmentation" is below this minimum, the dialog stops with a message stating exactly how many more runs are required. A small number of runs beyond the bare minimum is also recommended so some residual degrees of freedom remain for lack-of-fit testing and diagnostics — a design with exactly the minimum number of runs can fit the model but cannot check it.

Where the search region comes from
New candidate points are generated within the range already spanned by your existing design (the minimum and maximum of each component across its existing runs) — not a wider region you'd need to specify separately. If you need to search a genuinely larger region than your existing design covers, use Create D-Optimal Mixture Design instead with wider bounds.

Use an ODD candidate grid resolution
Same requirement as Create D-Optimal Mixture Design: an even resolution cannot represent an exact 50/50 binary blend (Total/2), and the search will substitute the nearest available fraction instead. Keep the resolution odd (default: 11).

Requires the 'AlgDesign' R package.
